The feeling of having done something wrong isn't evidence — it's the same discomfort as the four seconds, just longer. It shows up whether or not anything's actually wrong.

Something to do with your hands helps more than a mantra: keep them on the table, take a drink. Gives the gap somewhere to sit that isn't your mouth.

And you'll need a way back in when the quiet ends, because it will end. Something plain, like "that's the whole of it" or "I just wanted you to hear it from me." Not the gutters. The gutters are the fast talk.

So: tonight, the sentence that starts with you, then stop. Tuesday, the six words. Both the same move — plain, once, no filling.

Come back and tell me how tonight lands.
